title: Goal Decomposition
description: Break big tasks into steps. Help agents plan before they act.

title: Decision Trees
description: When to take which action. How agents choose their path.

title: Backtracking & Recovery
description: Handle failures gracefully. Let agents recover from mistakes.

title: Multi-Agent Systems
description: Agents talking to agents. Orchestrate complex workflows.

title: Evaluating Plans Before Execution
description: Catching a bad plan before the agent acts on it, not after.

title: Decomposition
description: Break a goal into steps that can be executed and verified independently — separating a goal from a task from a step, giving every step a completion condition you can actually check, telling real dependency apart from steps that only look independent, and replanning cleanly when one step fails instead of restarting from scratch.

title: Choosing an Approach
description: Make an agent pick a sensible strategy rather than the first one it thought of — generating real alternatives, running cheap checks before expensive work, knowing when to cut losses on an approach that isn't working, and leaving behind a record of why it chose what it chose.

title: Self-Checking
description: Build checking into a run without it becoming self-congratulation — asking an agent to review its own work, why that review tends to just agree, verifying against the actual artefact instead of the agent's own narrative about it, splitting critic and worker into separate roles that don't share context, and sizing every check against what the mistake it catches would actually cost.

title: Adapting to Reality
description: Handle the situation where the world isn't what the plan assumed — noticing where a plan's assumptions meet the actual environment, detecting that a specific assumption was wrong rather than just that something failed, choosing between adapting in place and starting over, deciding what partial progress is worth keeping, and reporting what changed and why instead of quietly rewriting history.

title: More Than One Agent
description: Decide when multiple agents genuinely help and coordinate them without chaos — recognizing when a single agent has actually run out of runway, splitting work between an orchestrator and workers, passing context between agents without losing what matters, getting independent perspectives that aren't just the same reasoning duplicated, and budgeting for the cost multiplier a second agent actually adds.
